speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of your cough, and do you have any fever or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Chest_XRay.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 9,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Chest_X_Ray: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any worsening with exertion? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary_Function_Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulmonary_Function_Tests: Reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, indicating a restrictive pattern.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you been exposed to any environmental toxins, such as asbestos or bird droppings, and do you have a history of autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune_Panel, Environmental_Exposure_History.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is surprising given the X-ray findings; could you describe your specific occupational history or hobbies in detail to rule out specific toxin exposures? Have you noticed any joint pain, skin rashes, or muscle weakness alongside your breathing issues? REQUEST TEST: High_Resolution_CT_Chest, Autoimmune_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis. The normal autoimmune and environmental workup, combined with the restrictive lung pattern and bilateral interstitial infiltrates, points to a diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
